subject: Audit & Access Log export options, retention windows and residency constraints
messages:
From: Priyanka Rao <prianka@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: security@atlas-payments.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Audit/access log retention & export for EU residency

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

We're finalizing our compliance matrix for Atlas Payments' deployment and need clarity on Redwood's audit and access log capabilities for EU-residency workloads. Two specific asks: 

1) What are the default retention windows for (a) audit logs (admin actions, rollouts, role changes) and (b) access logs (API request logs, token usage) in the hosted product?

2) Can we export full audit/access logs to our S3 bucket in eu-west-1? If so: format, compression, per-day chunking, encryption-at-rest options (customer-managed keys), and support for legal-hold (stop deletion) on exported objects.

We're trying to scope our data retention policy and any procurement amendments required to extend retention beyond defaults. A quick table or bullets would be great.

Thanks — Priyanka
Priyanka Rao
Head of Security — Atlas Payments
security@atlas-payments.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <prianka@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, security@atlas-payments.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit/access log retention & export for EU residency

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; forwarding internal implementation notes to Marissa and our infra team for any follow-ups (attached: redwood_audit_export_options.pdf).

- Defaults: hosted (multi-tenant) keeps structured access logs (API request metadata, response codes, latencies) for 90 days by default; audit logs (admin actions, policy changes, user provisioning) are retained 365 days by default.
- Extending retention: Dedicated and Private deployments support custom retention windows; for Hosted we offer paid retention extensions (e.g., 365/730/1095 days) under a retention addendum.
- Exports: yes — we support scheduled exports to customer S3 buckets in-region (eu-west-1). Exports are delivered as gzipped JSONL files, chunked by hour/day depending on volume. Files are signed (SHA256) and include a manifest with byte ranges.
- Encryption / KMS: exports can be written using Redwood-managed KMS keys or customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS. We support SSE-KMS and SSE-C either at export time or via pre-signed upload workflow.
- Legal hold / deletion controls: exported objects remain under customer control in their S3 bucket. For Hosted-native retention, we enforce deletion policies on Redwood's storage; legal holds should be implemented on the exported copy. We can support export hooks that snapshot on-demand when a legal hold is triggered.
- Residency: for EU residency, exports are routed to the requested region. Note: hosting metadata (control plane events) may still have pointers in the control plane; we can provide per-tenant manifests that avoid including customer PII if requested.

Next steps: Marissa, can your team confirm whether Atlas needs hashed identifiers only (no raw user ids) and whether they require exports buffered for an additional 30 days in our staging export bucket prior to delivery?

Best,
Jonas
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_audit_export_options.pdf (7 pages; export formats, example S3 policy, sample manifest)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit/access log retention & export for EU residency (internal follow-up)

Looping Sergio for the runtime/export mechanics and Laura for compliance sign-off. Quick tech notes for our answer to Atlas: 

- Export cadence options: hourly (default for high-volume tenants), daily (low-volume), on-demand snapshot. Files are emitted as JSONL, each line is a single event with standardized schema (timestamp, tenant_id_hash, request_id, method, path, status, latency_ms, node_id).
- PII minimization: we can provide a redaction layer that strips or hashes user identifiers before export; hashing is HMAC with tenant-specific salt to allow cross-file correlation without revealing raw IDs.
- Manifest & checksums: each export set includes manifest.json (export_start, export_end, file_list, checksums) and a signed manifest signature file.
- Retention & deletion: exports in customer buckets are subject to their lifecycle rules. For Hosted retention enforcement on Redwood side, deletions are triggered by our retention policy engine; we can provide a deletion log for auditing.
- Bandwidth & rate limits: large exports (multi-TB) should be arranged with pre-signed multipart uploads; we offer an accelerated delivery option for a bandwidth SLA.

Sergio — can you confirm encryption options we support for SSE-C and whether our signed upload flow supports customer KMS key IDs? Also include a sample aws s3 cp command to fetch a 24h export.

-Marissa

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit/access log retention & export for EU residency (technical detail)

Marissa / team — confirmed:

- KMS & SSE: we support SSE-KMS with customer key IDs (AWS) and SSE-C uploads for one-off encrypted payloads. For streamed exports we use SSE-KMS; CLI example to download a daily export (after presigned URL generation):

aws s3 cp "s3://atlas-exports-us-east-1/redwood/exports/2026-06-15/export-2026-06-15-00-23.jsonl.gz" - | gunzip -c > audit-20260615.jsonl

- Signed manifests: our export service will POST manifest and signature to a callback endpoint (if provided) or place them in the same bucket.
- On-demand snapshot: API /v1/exports/snapshots supports specifying time range + redaction=hash|strip and retention_override_days parameter (max 3650 days for enterprise contracts).
- Deletion & legal hold workflow: we support a webhook that can be invoked by a customer legal team to create a snapshot and to pause internal deletion for a tenant for up to 90 days while a support ticket is open; longer holds require an SSO-signed request and an internal compliance review.

I'll assemble a concise step-by-step we can send to Priyanka, including the minimal IAM policy they should attach to the S3 upload role.

-Sergio

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <prianka@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, security@atlas-payments.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit/access log retention & export for EU residency

Hi Priyanka — quick action plan and answers based on the notes above: 

1) Defaults: Access logs = 90 days; Audit logs = 365 days (hosted). Dedicated/Private or retention addendum required for longer hosted retention.
2) Exports: Supported to eu-west-1 S3. Format = gzipped JSONL. Chunking configurable (hourly/daily).
3) Encryption: SSE-KMS with CMKs supported (we can accept key IDs). Signed manifests and checksums included.
4) PII / residency: We can export hashed identifiers (HMAC with tenant salt) or strip fields entirely. Exports are generated in-region.
5) Legal hold / long-term: Exports are customer-managed in their bucket; for hosting-side holds we offer a webhook-driven snapshot and 90-day pause on deletion (longer requires contract amendment).

Attached: signed_export_instructions.txt (includes sample IAM policy, presigned URL flow, and recommended lifecycle rules for Atlas).

If that covers it, let's schedule a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through the sample export and IAM role. I'll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Jonas
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: signed_export_instructions.txt (2 pages; sample IAM, presigned upload flow)
